original_query: weakest topology making every evaluation map continuous
original_context: General topology: initial topology on a set X induced by maps f_i:X→(Y_i,τ_i) into topological spaces, namely the coarsest topology on X for which every f_i is continuous; it is generated by the family of all preimages f_i^{-1}[U] with U∈τ_i.
definition: Let X be a set and (f_i:X→Y_i)_{i∈I} be maps to topological spaces (Y_i,τ_i). The initial topology on X generated by these maps is the coarsest topology on X making every f_i continuous; a subbase is {f_i^{-1}(U):i∈I,U∈τ_i}.
reasoning: This general initial-topology construction is not identical to the screened product topology: product topology is its specialization using coordinate projections; the screened Krull topology is another specialization by Galois evaluation maps. It provides a genuine independent general definition with no requirement of injectivity or surjectivity of the maps.

mathematical_assumptions: No injectivity or jointly separating points required.
When I is empty, the initial topology is indiscrete {∅,X}.
If X is empty the indiscrete topology has only the empty set.
